# Dataset Dictionary: EconoCausal Synthetic Pricing Data

**Maintained by:** Member 1 (Data) | **Generated by:** `generate_synthetic.py` (seed 42) | **Cleaned by:** `clean_and_engineer.py`

This is a **simulated** shop. The effects of discounts in it are set by us, not measured in the real world.

## Files

| File | Rows | Columns | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/synthetic/synthetic_pricing.csv` | 20,000 | 11 | Raw synthetic data |
| `data/processed/synthetic_pricing_clean.csv` | 20,000 | 14 | Validated data plus engineered features. **Use this for modelling** |
| `data/synthetic/synthetic_ground_truth.csv` | 20,000 | 6 | True effects (answer key). **Evaluation only** |

## Columns in the pricing data

| Column | Type | Values | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | text | CUST_00001 to CUST_20000 | Identifier | Unique customer. Not a feature |
| `age` | integer | 18 to 65 | X | Customer age in years |
| `region` | category | North, South, East, West, Central | X | Customer region |
| `monthly_income` | integer | about 5,000 to 377,000 | X | Monthly income in INR (rounded to nearest 100) |
| `loyalty_member` | 0/1 | 1 = loyalty member | X | Member before the campaign |
| `past_purchases` | integer | 0 to 14 | X | Purchases made before the campaign |
| `days_since_last_purchase` | integer | 1 to 365 | X | Days since the customer's previous purchase, before the campaign |
| `avg_basket_value` | integer | about 16 to 1,800 | X | Typical basket value in INR before any discount |
| `discount` | integer | 0, 10, 20 | T (treatment) | Discount offered in INR |
| `purchased` | 0/1 | 1 = bought | Y (outcome) | Whether the customer purchased after the offer |
| `spend` | integer | 0 and above | Not a feature | Amount spent in INR (0 if no purchase). Measured **after** the discount |

## Engineered columns (clean file only)

| Column | Built from | Rule | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `age_group` | `age` | 18-29 young, 30-49 adult, 50+ older | X |
| `income_tier` | `monthly_income` | up to 20,000 low, 20,001-50,000 medium, above 50,000 high | X |
| `recency_group` | `days_since_last_purchase` | up to 15 recent, 16-45 moderate, above 45 lapsed | X |

All three use only information known before the discount, so they do not leak the treatment or outcome.

## Ground-truth file (answer key)

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `customer_id` | Links to the pricing data |
| `true_prob_discount_0`, `_10`, `_20` | The customer's true purchase probability under each discount |
| `true_uplift_10`, `true_uplift_20` | True increase in purchase probability versus no discount (probability scale) |

## Rules for using this data

| Rule | Reason |
|---|---|
| Features (X) must be pre-treatment columns only | Prevents leakage |
| Never use `discount`, `purchased` or `spend` as features | They are the treatment and the outcome or come after them |
| Never use the ground-truth file for training or choosing offers | Evaluation only |
| Do not use `customer_id` as a feature | It is an identifier |

## Treatment assignment (important for causal analysis)

Discounts are **not random**. Customers with more past purchases and more recent activity are offered larger discounts more often, and those customers also buy more anyway. This confounding is intentional. A naive comparison overstates the effect: it shows about a 15 point rise in purchase rate for Rs 10 (40.3% to 55.0%), while the true average effect is about 10 points.

## Known quality checks (see `docs/cleaning_report.md`)

12 validation rules were run on the raw file. No missing values, duplicates or invalid values were found, and no rows were excluded.

## Limitations

- Simulated data: effects are built in by the generator and are not real-world evidence.
- The same customers have no repeated observations (one row per customer).
- Treatment effects are defined on the probability scale, and `spend` is not modelled causally.
